rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The paper provides detailed description of M-ComBat harmonization. The HCP-YA was used as reference site. The external StratiBip test set HC portion (N=363) was concatenated with HCP-YA training set to estimate site effects, which were then applied to harmonize all test data (both HC and BD). Age, sex, and TIV were preserved as biological covariates. Comprehensive validation was performed including statistical tests, SVM classification, and biological covariate preservation checks. The harmonization was specifically designed for external validation framework. M-ComBat harmonization method; batch variable = site (7 StratiBip sites harmonized to HCP-YA reference); covariates preserved = age, sex, TIV (for volume features); external test set HC portion used to estimate site effects with reference training set; harmonization validated through: (1) Kruskal-Wallis ANOVA comparing feature distributions across sites pre/post harmonization, (2) SVM site classification showing decreased performance post-harmonization (f1-score from 95% to 23%), (3) preservation of biological covariates assessed via linear regression models; out-of-sample harmonization framework for external validation
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We propose an innovative pipeline to enable site harmonization of non-normative external datasets with the normative training set... In this case, the M-ComBat model was fitted exclusively on a normative sample and later applied to all test data. First, the external test set (StratiBip) HC portion ( N = 363), yij = HC , v , is concatenated with the HCP-YA normative training set, which was used as the reference i = HCP to estimate the StratiBip site-effects... For all feature sets, age and sex were included as biocovariates to preserve, while for volume features, previously harmonized TIV was also included... To ascertain the harmonization success, we proceed with a series of validation analyses... Before harmonization, all feature set distributions (GMV, WMV, CT) for the HCs among the 8 sites (HCP site and 7 StratiBip sites) resulted significantly different ( p < 1e-29 ) but no differences were detected among sites after harmonization ( p > 0.680 )... A substantial decline in average f1-score was observed in the validation portion (N = 836), from 95 % before harmonization to 23 % after harmonization

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: BD shows higher and more heterogeneous deviations than HC with increased extreme values; significant deviations localize notably to basal ganglia, hippocampus, and adjacent regions; individualized mZ-based maps show higher abnormality occurrences but lower spatial overlap in BD.
